note: `test: null` — the whole suite. The change is three switch arms and a
vocabulary rule, and the discriminating assertions live in
raster_colour_test.dart; running everything is what proves nothing *else*
was holding the old throw in place.
The two `reverts to the throw` cases are this ticket's own test-trust gate
made permanent: each puts back the exact behaviour #64 removed, so a green
run would mean the flipped tests never discriminated.
`none is filed as unreadable` is the acceptance criterion's mutation. Since
#64 it is *output-neutral everywhere* — both states paint nothing in a
fill and black in a stop-color — so only the type-level assertions in
raster_colour_test.dart can kill it. That is deliberate (see the
ColourDeclaration doc): the day a property answers the two differently
again, the types are the only thing standing between the collapse and a
The two `white` cases are the acceptance criterion's other mutation: the
black is a derived initial value (ADR-0001 R2), not a taste, and white is
the nearest wrong constant — for the absent case it is also the value the
empty-palette golden (`sunset` solid black disc, hidden-state #39) pins.
